2. Facts, necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No.204 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Mymensingh for declaration that the record of rights prepared in the name of the defendant relates to the suit schedule property is wrong and for a further declaration of title in the suit schedule 2 property measuring 2.14 decimals of land contending inter alia that in 30.32 decimals of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.199, Jagmohan Namadash and Harimohan Namadash had one ana share each. Said Jagamohan Namodash died leaving 2 sons Motiram and Sutiram who inherited 7.08 

 acres of land in the suit schedule property. Sutiram died leaving 2 sons Jogesh and Umesh, predecessor of defendant Nos.1 and 2-4 respectively. MotiraM died leaving 2 daughters plaintiff No.1 Sumitra and Niroda, mother of defendant Nos.5 and 6. The Plaintiff No.1 inherited 1.891/2 acres of land with limited right. Defendant Nos.5 and 6 inherited same portion' of land as inherited by the plaintiff No.1. Plaintiff No.2 acquired .25 decimals of land from Plot No.1234 described in suit schedule No.2 vide a deed of exchange dated 9.3.1989 and thus the plaintiffs became owners of 2.141/2 acres of land. The S.A. record is wrong and plaintiffs came to know about the wrong recording of S.A. Khatian on 3.5.1986 after obtaining certified copy of the parcha and thereafter instituted the present suit. 

 7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Shankar Chandra Das, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in holding that the plea of deed of gift is nothing but a myth without considering that the trial Court arrived at a finding that the record of right was prepared pursuant to the deed of gift and Motiram used to live his father-in-law's house and never claimed the suit property during his life time. The learned Advocate also submits that the Subordinate Judge failed to consider the legal aspect of the case that as the plaintiffs did not claim the entire property of Motiram the suit is not maintainable under Order 2 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate next submits that the cause of action of the suit arose from the wrong record of S.A. Khatian which was finally published in the year 1963 and as such the suit is barred under Article 102 of the Limitation Act.
